title: Se présenter
intro: Short, friendly sentences to start. Listen for the silent endings you can't hear but must write.

sentences.fr: Bonjour, je m'appelle Marie.
sentences.en: Hello, my name is Marie.
sentences.tip: « je m'appelle » — two p's, two l's, and don't forget the apostrophe.

sentences.fr: Comment allez-vous aujourd'hui ?
sentences.en: How are you today?
sentences.tip: Hear the liaison: « allez‿vous ». And « aujourd'hui » hides a silent d.

sentences.fr: J'habite à Paris depuis deux ans.
sentences.en: I've been living in Paris for two years.
sentences.tip: Liaison « deux‿ans » sounds like a z — but you still write « deux ans ».

sentences.fr: Nous sommes très contents de vous voir.
sentences.en: We're very happy to see you.
sentences.tip: « contents » is plural — the silent -s agrees with « nous ».

sentences.fr: Il fait beau ce matin.
sentences.en: The weather is nice this morning.
sentences.tip: « ce matin », not « se matin » — a classic homophone trap.

title: Les chiffres et l'heure
intro: Numbers and times are where listening points are won or lost. Train them on purpose.

sentences.fr: Il est huit heures et quart.
sentences.en: It's a quarter past eight.
sentences.tip: Liaison « huit‿heures ».

sentences.fr: J'ai soixante-dix euros dans mon sac.
sentences.en: I have seventy euros in my bag.
sentences.tip: 70 = soixante-dix (sixty-ten). Hyphenated.

sentences.fr: Il y a quatre-vingts personnes dans la salle.
sentences.en: There are eighty people in the room.
sentences.tip: 80 = quatre-vingts — with an -s when it ends the number.

sentences.fr: Le rendez-vous est à quinze heures trente.
sentences.en: The appointment is at 3:30 p.m.
sentences.tip: 15 h 30 spoken in full. Liaison « quinze‿heures ».

sentences.fr: Mon train part à neuf heures moins le quart.
sentences.en: My train leaves at a quarter to nine.
sentences.tip: Liaison « neuf‿heures » — here the f sounds like a v.

title: Quelle heure est-il ?
intro: The clock is full of endings you can hear perfectly and still write wrong. Listen especially for whether « demi » takes an -e — it depends on the word in front of it.

sentences.fr: Quelle heure est-il ? Il est bientôt minuit.
sentences.en: What time is it? It's nearly midnight.
sentences.tip: « quelle » agrees with the feminine heure — two l's and an -e. est-il takes a hyphen, and minuit hides a silent t.

sentences.fr: Il est midi et demi, on déjeune ?
sentences.en: It's half past twelve, shall we have lunch?
sentences.tip: No -e on demi here: midi is masculine. Same for « minuit et demi ».

sentences.fr: Le film dure une heure et demie.
sentences.en: The film lasts an hour and a half.
sentences.tip: Now demie takes the -e, because it agrees with the feminine heure. dure, not dur — it's the verb.

sentences.fr: Je serai là dans un quart d'heure.
sentences.en: I'll be there in a quarter of an hour.
sentences.tip: « un quart d'heure » is a length of time: three words and an apostrophe. Don't confuse it with « et quart » on the clock.

sentences.fr: Le train part à dix-huit heures quarante-cinq.
sentences.en: The train leaves at 18:45.
sentences.tip: Both numbers keep their hyphens, and quarante has a single t. The 24-hour clock never says « moins le quart ».

title: En ville
intro: Places, shops and directions. Most of the marks here are in the little words — the article, and whether de merges with le.

sentences.fr: La boulangerie est en face de la poste.
sentences.en: The bakery is opposite the post office.
sentences.tip: Every -erie shop is feminine, so « la boulangerie ». « en face de » stays separate before la.

sentences.fr: Tournez à gauche après l'église.
sentences.en: Turn left after the church.
sentences.tip: « à » takes the accent grave. église hides its gender behind l' — it's feminine.

sentences.fr: Il y a une pharmacie près du parc.
sentences.en: There's a pharmacy near the park.
sentences.tip: « près du » is près de + le, merged. Three separate words in « il y a ».

sentences.fr: Je vais à la mairie pour mes papiers.
sentences.en: I'm going to the town hall for my paperwork.
sentences.tip: à la, not au — mairie is feminine. mes because papiers is plural.

sentences.fr: Le musée est au troisième étage.
sentences.en: The museum is on the third floor.
sentences.tip: Ordinals end in -ième. « au » = à + le, and étage takes an accent aigu.

title: Les transports
intro: The preposition is the whole game: en for transport you get inside, à for transport you sit on — and never an article after either.

sentences.fr: Je vais au travail en bus.
sentences.en: I go to work by bus.
sentences.tip: « en bus » — no article. « en le bus » does not exist.

sentences.fr: Elle vient en voiture.
sentences.en: She's coming by car.
sentences.tip: vient ends in a silent -t. voiture has no circumflex.

sentences.fr: Nous allons à l'université à vélo.
sentences.en: We go to university by bike.
sentences.tip: Two different à in one sentence: « à l'université » is the place, « à vélo » is the transport.

sentences.fr: Tu rentres à pied ?
sentences.en: Are you walking home?
sentences.tip: The -es of rentres is silent but must be written. « à pied » stays singular.

sentences.fr: Ils prennent le tramway tous les matins.
sentences.en: They take the tram every morning.
sentences.tip: prennent — double n, and -ent is silent. With prendre the article comes back: le tramway.

title: Le présent — les terminaisons muettes
intro: The hardest dictation in French: endings you cannot hear but have to write. « il regarde » and « ils regardent » sound identical — only the sentence tells you which.

sentences.fr: Je mange une pomme.
sentences.en: I'm eating an apple.
sentences.tip: The -e of mange is silent and still compulsory. 1st group.

sentences.fr: Ils regardent la télévision.
sentences.en: They're watching television.
sentences.tip: The classic trap: -ent is completely silent, so « regardent » sounds exactly like « regarde ». Only ils tells you.

sentences.fr: Nous finissons nos devoirs.
sentences.en: We're finishing our homework.
sentences.tip: 2nd group: the -iss- shows up in the plural. nos, because devoirs is plural.

sentences.fr: Vous choisissez toujours la meilleure place.
sentences.en: You always choose the best seat.
sentences.tip: choisissez — the -iss- then -ez. meilleure takes two l and an -eure.

sentences.fr: Elle va à l'école tous les jours.
sentences.en: She goes to school every day.
sentences.tip: va has no -s. « tous les jours » — the s of tous is silent here.

title: Ma famille
intro: Possessives are chosen by the thing owned, not the owner — so listen to the noun, not to who's speaking.

sentences.fr: Mon frère habite à Lyon avec sa femme.
sentences.en: My brother lives in Lyon with his wife.
sentences.tip: sa agrees with femme, not with the brother. That's why « sa femme » can be his or her wife.

sentences.fr: Ma sœur travaille à l'hôpital.
sentences.en: My sister works at the hospital.
sentences.tip: sœur uses the œ ligature. hôpital keeps its circumflex.

sentences.fr: Mes parents viennent nous voir en août.
sentences.en: My parents are coming to see us in August.
sentences.tip: mes for plural. viennent — double n and a silent -ent.

sentences.fr: Mon amie Claire est très gentille.
sentences.en: My friend Claire is very kind.
sentences.tip: mon amie, not ma amie — a feminine word starting with a vowel takes mon. But gentille stays feminine.

sentences.fr: Nos enfants vont à l'école du quartier.
sentences.en: Our children go to the local school.
sentences.tip: nos for plural. vont has no -ent. « du quartier » is de + le.

title: Dire non
intro: The ne is barely audible in normal speech — but it always has to be written. That's the whole exercise.

sentences.fr: Je ne veux pas aller là-bas.
sentences.en: I don't want to go there.
sentences.tip: Both halves: ne before the verb, pas after. « là-bas » takes a hyphen and an accent grave.

sentences.fr: Ne pas marcher sur le gazon.
sentences.en: Do not walk on the grass.
sentences.tip: No conjugated verb, so ne and pas stay together in front of the infinitive. The sign form.

sentences.fr: Elle n'a plus faim.
sentences.en: She isn't hungry anymore.
sentences.tip: ne shortens to n' before a vowel. plus for « anymore » — and no article before faim.

sentences.fr: Je ne mange pas de fromage.
sentences.en: I don't eat cheese.
sentences.tip: After a negative, du collapses to a bare de. Never « pas du fromage » here.

sentences.fr: Il n'y a personne dans la rue.
sentences.en: There's nobody in the street.
sentences.tip: personne replaces pas as the second half. « il n'y a » — three little words, easy to run together.

title: Le visage
intro: Describing a face, and the article traps that come with it. Listen for whether the noun is singular or plural — the sound often won't tell you.

sentences.fr: Elle a les yeux bleus et les cheveux courts.
sentences.en: She has blue eyes and short hair.
sentences.tip: les, not ses — French uses the definite article for body parts. bleus and courts both take the plural -s.

sentences.fr: J'entends la musique mais je n'écoute pas.
sentences.en: I can hear the music but I'm not listening.
sentences.tip: entends ends in a silent -s. n'écoute — the apostrophe replaces the e of ne.

sentences.fr: Il a mal à la tête depuis ce matin.
sentences.en: He's had a headache since this morning.
sentences.tip: « à la tête », never « à sa tête ». depuis, not depuit.

sentences.fr: Nous voyons la mer depuis la fenêtre.
sentences.en: We can see the sea from the window.
sentences.tip: voir becomes voy- at nous. « la mer » — the sea, not la mère.

sentences.fr: Ça sent bon dans la cuisine.
sentences.en: It smells good in the kitchen.
sentences.tip: sent with a silent -t. bon stays masculine singular here — it's describing the smell, not the kitchen.

title: Le corps et « avoir mal »
intro: Saying what hurts, and the little words that come with it. Listen for whether the body part is singular or plural — au or aux sound almost the same, and only one of them is right.

sentences.fr: J'ai mal au dos depuis trois jours.
sentences.en: My back has hurt for three days.
sentences.tip: à + le contracts to au, one word. dos ends in a silent -s even in the singular.

sentences.fr: Le médecin regarde mon épaule gauche.
sentences.en: The doctor is looking at my left shoulder.
sentences.tip: épaule is feminine, but it takes mon, not ma — French uses the masculine form before a vowel. gauche agrees with it.

sentences.fr: Elle a mal aux jambes et aux pieds.
sentences.en: Her legs and feet hurt.
sentences.tip: aux is the plural of au, and both nouns carry an -s you cannot hear.

sentences.fr: Lave-toi les mains avant de manger.
sentences.en: Wash your hands before eating.
sentences.tip: The hyphen is compulsory in the imperative. And « les mains », never « tes mains » — French uses the plain article for your own body.

sentences.fr: J'ai mal au cœur en voiture.
sentences.en: I feel sick in the car.
sentences.tip: cœur is written with the ligature œ. And it means to feel nauseous — nothing to do with the heart.

title: Hier, maintenant, demain
intro: Five sentences that place themselves in time. Listen for whether it's « il y a » or « dans » — one small word sends the sentence backwards or forwards.

sentences.fr: Maintenant, j'habite à Paris.
sentences.en: Now I live in Paris.
sentences.tip: The h of habiter is silent, so the apostrophe is compulsory: j'habite, never « je habite ».

sentences.fr: Nous sommes arrivés il y a huit mois.
sentences.en: We arrived eight months ago.
sentences.tip: « il y a » is three separate words. mois keeps its -s even in the singular.

sentences.fr: Après-demain, je vais voir un ami.
sentences.en: The day after tomorrow, I'm going to see a friend.
sentences.tip: Après-demain takes a hyphen and an accent grave; the -s of après stays silent.

sentences.fr: La semaine prochaine, on va déménager.
sentences.en: Next week we're going to move house.
sentences.tip: prochaine agrees with the feminine semaine, so the -e. déménager: two accents aigus, both é.

sentences.fr: Actuellement, je cherche un appartement.
sentences.en: I'm currently looking for a flat.
sentences.tip: Two l's in actuellement — and it means currently, not « actually ». appartement doubles the p, not the t.

title: Depuis, pendant, il y a
intro: Five sentences that say how long. Listen for which word arrives — depuis, pendant, il y a or dans — because each one drags a different tense along with it.

sentences.fr: J'habite en France depuis huit mois.
sentences.en: I've been living in France for eight months.
sentences.tip: depuis always ends in a silent -s. The verb stays in the present, because you still live there — no past tense here.

sentences.fr: J'ai travaillé pendant trois ans à Delhi.
sentences.en: I worked for three years in Delhi.
sentences.tip: pendant ends in a silent -t. travaillé is the participle, so -é and not -er.

sentences.fr: Ça fait deux heures que je t'attends !
sentences.en: I've been waiting for you for two hours!
sentences.tip: « Ça » takes a cedilla. t'attends has the apostrophe and a silent -s you must still write.

sentences.fr: Nous partons en vacances dans une semaine.
sentences.en: We're going on holiday in a week.
sentences.tip: dans, not « d'en ». And « en vacances » is always written in the plural.

sentences.fr: Je n'ai pas vu mes parents depuis Noël.
sentences.en: I haven't seen my parents since Christmas.
sentences.tip: n'ai — the apostrophe replaces the e of ne. Noël keeps its tréma on the e.

title: Les mois et la date
intro: Months in lower case, days as plain numbers, and years written as one long word-chain. The dictation is where the capital letters give you away.

sentences.fr: Aujourd'hui, on est le six août.
sentences.en: Today is the sixth of August.
sentences.tip: No capital on août, and no de: « le six août », never « le sixième d'août ».

sentences.fr: Mon anniversaire, c'est le premier mai.
sentences.en: My birthday is the first of May.
sentences.tip: premier is the only ordinal a date ever takes. anniversaire: two n's, one s in the middle.

sentences.fr: Nous sommes arrivés en décembre deux mille vingt-cinq.
sentences.en: We arrived in December 2025.
sentences.tip: en before the month. The year is one number: deux mille vingt-cinq, with a hyphen only in vingt-cinq.

sentences.fr: Le rendez-vous est le douze mars à quatorze heures.
sentences.en: The appointment is on the twelfth of March at two p.m.
sentences.tip: rendez-vous is hyphenated. The -s of mars is pronounced, and quatorze‿heures links into one sound.

sentences.fr: En juillet et en août, beaucoup de magasins sont fermés.
sentences.en: In July and August, a lot of shops are closed.
sentences.tip: juillet has a double l. août keeps its circumflex, and « en août » runs together as « ah-noot ».

title: Je me lève, nous nous levons
intro: These verbs are mostly a spelling problem. Listen for whether the little pronoun is there, and count the l's before you write appeler.

sentences.fr: Je me lève à sept heures tous les matins.
sentences.en: I get up at seven every morning.
sentences.tip: Two words before the verb: je, then me. lève takes an accent grave — you can hear it, « LEV ».

sentences.fr: Nous nous levons tôt le dimanche.
sentences.en: We get up early on Sundays.
sentences.tip: nous really is written twice: the subject, then the pronoun. And levons has no accent — « luh-VOHN ».

sentences.fr: Comment vous appelez-vous ?
sentences.en: What's your name?
sentences.tip: One l in appelez, and the second vous is hyphenated onto the verb in this question form.

sentences.fr: Ils s'appellent Marc et Julie.
sentences.en: They're called Marc and Julie.
sentences.tip: Two l's here, because you hear « a-PEL ». The apostrophe replaces the e of se.

sentences.fr: Je ne me couche pas avant minuit.
sentences.en: I don't go to bed before midnight.
sentences.tip: The ne comes before me, not before the verb: ne me couche pas. minuit ends in a silent -t.

title: Les pays et les nationalités
intro: Countries take a capital letter, nationalities don't, and the feminine ending is often the only part you can actually hear. All three get tested here.

sentences.fr: Je suis indienne et j'habite en France.
sentences.en: I'm Indian and I live in France.
sentences.tip: indienne doubles the n in the feminine, with no capital. France is feminine, so « en France » — never « à la France ».

sentences.fr: Mon mari vient du Canada.
sentences.en: My husband comes from Canada.
sentences.tip: Canada is masculine, so de + le contracts to du. The country keeps its capital C.

sentences.fr: Nous allons aux États-Unis en septembre.
sentences.en: We're going to the United States in September.
sentences.tip: aux for a plural country. États-Unis: capital É, capital U, and a hyphen between them.

sentences.fr: Elle est allemande, mais elle parle très bien français.
sentences.en: She's German, but she speaks French very well.
sentences.tip: allemande — the -e is what makes the d audible. After parler the language takes no article: « parle français ».

sentences.fr: Il y a beaucoup de touristes japonais à Paris.
sentences.en: There are a lot of Japanese tourists in Paris.
sentences.tip: japonais already ends in -s, so the masculine plural adds nothing. A city takes plain à.

title: Les métiers
intro: Two things to watch: whether the job takes an article at all, and the feminine ending, which is often the only part you can hear.

sentences.fr: Ma sœur est infirmière dans un hôpital.
sentences.en: My sister is a nurse in a hospital.
sentences.tip: No article after est. infirmière takes an accent grave, and hôpital keeps its circumflex.

sentences.fr: Il est boulanger et sa femme est boulangère.
sentences.en: He's a baker and his wife is a baker.
sentences.tip: The -ère ending is the only audible difference between them. Still no article, either time.

sentences.fr: C'est une avocate très connue.
sentences.en: She's a very well-known lawyer.
sentences.tip: After c'est the article comes back: une. Both avocate and connue take the feminine -e.

sentences.fr: Je cherche un travail dans l'informatique.
sentences.en: I'm looking for a job in IT.
sentences.tip: travail ends in -ail with no -e. l'informatique is feminine, and the article elides before the vowel.

sentences.fr: Je travaille chez Renault depuis trois ans.
sentences.en: I've been working at Renault for three years.
sentences.tip: chez never changes and its -z is silent. depuis ends in a silent -s, and « trois ans » links with a z.

title: Toujours, souvent, jamais
intro: Listen for where the little word lands — it comes after the verb, not before it. And every one of these hides a silent letter at the end.

sentences.fr: Je vais souvent au marché le samedi.
sentences.en: I often go to the market on Saturdays.
sentences.tip: souvent sits after the verb, and its final -t is silent. « le samedi » means every Saturday.

sentences.fr: Elle ne mange jamais de viande.
sentences.en: She never eats meat.
sentences.tip: ne … jamais wraps the verb like ne … pas, and « de la viande » collapses to a bare de after a negative.

sentences.fr: Nous prenons rarement le train.
sentences.en: We rarely take the train.
sentences.tip: rarement is built on the feminine rare plus -ment, so the e in the middle stays.

sentences.fr: De temps en temps, je fais la cuisine.
sentences.en: From time to time, I do the cooking.
sentences.tip: Three separate words, no hyphens — and temps keeps both its silent p and its silent s, twice.

sentences.fr: Il est toujours en retard.
sentences.en: He's always late.
sentences.tip: toujours always ends in -s, even about one person. « en retard » is two words.

title: La maison et le quotidien
intro: Everyday actions — watch the past-tense agreements and the reflexive verbs.

sentences.fr: Je me lève tôt et je prends mon café.
sentences.en: I get up early and have my coffee.
sentences.tip: « je me lève » — reflexive, with an accent grave.

sentences.fr: Les enfants jouent dans le jardin.
sentences.en: The children are playing in the garden.
sentences.tip: « jouent » — the -ent ending is completely silent.

sentences.fr: Nous avons acheté une nouvelle voiture.
sentences.en: We bought a new car.
sentences.tip: « acheté » here ends in -é (past participle), not -er.

sentences.fr: Elle est allée au marché ce week-end.
sentences.en: She went to the market this weekend.
sentences.tip: « allée » — with être, the participle agrees: extra -e for « elle ».

sentences.fr: Tu as oublié tes clés sur la table.
sentences.en: You left your keys on the table.
sentences.tip: « tes clés » — both are plural, both take a silent -s.

title: Le passé composé
intro: The tense where French hides most of its spelling. Almost none of the agreements can be heard — you have to work them out from the auxiliary and the subject.

sentences.fr: Hier, j'ai pris le métro et j'ai lu mon livre.
sentences.en: Yesterday I took the metro and read my book.
sentences.tip: pris ends in -s, lu in -u. Neither ending is audible; both simply have to be learnt.

sentences.fr: Elle est allée au marché et elle est rentrée tard.
sentences.en: She went to the market and came home late.
sentences.tip: Both verbs take être, so both participles agree with elle — two silent extra e's.

sentences.fr: Nous n'avons pas compris la question.
sentences.en: We didn't understand the question.
sentences.tip: The ne … pas wraps the auxiliary alone: « n'avons pas compris », never « n'avons compris pas ».

sentences.fr: Ils sont nés en Inde et ils sont arrivés en 2025.
sentences.en: They were born in India and arrived in 2025.
sentences.tip: être again, so both participles take the plural -s. nés keeps its accent aigu.

sentences.fr: J'ai dû partir avant la fin.
sentences.en: I had to leave before the end.
sentences.tip: dû wears its circumflex only in the masculine singular — it is there to keep it apart from « du ».

title: Le matin, au passé
intro: The agreement on these participles is completely silent — levé, levée, levés and levées are one sound. So this is pure writing practice. Ask yourself each time what the verb actually acted on.

sentences.fr: Ce matin, je me suis réveillée à six heures.
sentences.en: This morning I woke up at six.
sentences.tip: A woman writing, so réveillée takes the -e: with être the participle agrees with the subject.

sentences.fr: Je me suis lavé les mains avant de manger.
sentences.en: I washed my hands before eating.
sentences.tip: No -e this time. « les mains » comes after the verb, so nothing agrees — compare « je me suis lavée ».

sentences.fr: Elle s'est habillée et elle s'est brossé les dents.
sentences.en: She got dressed and brushed her teeth.
sentences.tip: habillée agrees, brossé does not — « les dents » follows the verb. And it is s'est, not c'est.

sentences.fr: Nous nous sommes couchés très tard hier soir.
sentences.en: We went to bed very late last night.
sentences.tip: The pronoun is written twice: nous nous. couchés takes the plural -s.

sentences.fr: Je ne me suis pas dépêché ce matin.
sentences.en: I didn't hurry this morning.
sentences.tip: The ne goes in front of the pronoun and the pas after être — four words before you reach the participle.

title: Quand j'étais petite
intro: The imparfait endings all sound the same — -ais, -ait and -aient are one noise. What you're really writing down is the person, which only the pronoun tells you. Two spelling traps hide in here as well.

sentences.fr: Quand j'étais petite, j'habitais en Inde.
sentences.en: When I was little, I lived in India.
sentences.tip: Both verbs take -ais for je. habitais keeps its silent h and takes no accent, unlike étais.

sentences.fr: Nous faisions du vélo tous les dimanches.
sentences.en: We used to cycle every Sunday.
sentences.tip: Said « fuh-ZYOHN » — the ai of faire says « uh ». And dimanches takes an -s: it happened every week.

sentences.fr: Pendant que je dormais, mon téléphone a sonné.
sentences.en: While I was sleeping, my phone rang.
sentences.tip: Two tenses on purpose: dormais is the backdrop, a sonné is the event. « Pendant que », two words.

sentences.fr: Vous étudiiez le français à l'époque ?
sentences.en: Were you studying French back then?
sentences.tip: Two i's in étudiiez — the stem ends in i and the ending adds another. You write both and say one.

sentences.fr: Je mangeais souvent au restaurant.
sentences.en: I often ate at restaurants.
sentences.tip: mangeais keeps the e of manger so the g stays soft before the a — exactly like nous mangeons.

title: Donner son avis
intro: The connectors and verb moods you'll need to argue a point — and the first taste of the subjunctive.

sentences.fr: À mon avis, il faudrait réduire la pollution.
sentences.en: In my opinion, we should reduce pollution.
sentences.tip: « faudrait » — conditional, silent -t.

sentences.fr: Beaucoup de gens pensent que c'est une bonne idée.
sentences.en: Many people think it's a good idea.
sentences.tip: « pensent » — silent -ent. « c'est », not « ses » or « ces ».

sentences.fr: Si j'avais le temps, je voyagerais davantage.
sentences.en: If I had time, I would travel more.
sentences.tip: si + imparfait, then conditional. « voyagerais » ends in -ais.

sentences.fr: Il est important que nous fassions un effort.
sentences.en: It's important that we make an effort.
sentences.tip: « que nous fassions » — subjunctive of faire. Liaison « un‿effort ».

sentences.fr: Les jeunes utilisent de plus en plus leur téléphone.
sentences.en: Young people use their phones more and more.
sentences.tip: « leur » stays singular here — one phone each, no -s.

title: Actualité et argumentation
intro: Full DELF-B2 register: abstract nouns, the subjunctive, and the agreements that separate B2 from B1.

sentences.fr: Bien qu'il soit difficile, ce changement est nécessaire.
sentences.en: Although it is difficult, this change is necessary.
sentences.tip: « Bien que » forces the subjunctive « soit ».

sentences.fr: Les autorités ont annoncé de nouvelles mesures économiques.
sentences.en: The authorities have announced new economic measures.
sentences.tip: « nouvelles mesures économiques » — three feminine plurals to agree.

sentences.fr: Cette décision aura des conséquences importantes pour l'avenir.
sentences.en: This decision will have major consequences for the future.
sentences.tip: « aura » — simple future. « conséquences importantes » both plural.

sentences.fr: Nombreux sont ceux qui s'inquiètent de la situation.
sentences.en: Many are those who worry about the situation.
sentences.tip: « s'inquiètent » — reflexive, silent -ent, accent grave on the è.

sentences.fr: Il ne faut pas négliger l'impact environnemental de nos choix.
sentences.en: We must not neglect the environmental impact of our choices.
sentences.tip: « environnemental » — double n, then -mental. A spelling trap even for natives.
